name: Death Certificate
department: Office of the Registrar General of India — Civil Registration System (CRS)
summary: Official proof of death registered with the local municipal or panchayat authority, required for insurance claims, property transfer, and closing the deceased's accounts.
eligibility: Every death occurring in India must be registered within 21 days, free of charge, by a family member, hospital, or local informant
Late registration is possible with a delay fee; registration after 1 year requires a magistrate/District Magistrate order
documents: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) for hospital deaths, or cremation/burial certificate
fee: Free within 21 days of death. ₹5-25 for delayed registration (22 days to 1 year); ₹25 plus a District Magistrate order for registration after 1 year.
process: Hospital or informant reports the death to the local registrar (municipal corporation/panchayat)
For online applications, register on your state's CRS/e-District portal and fill Form 2
Upload the MCCD/cremation certificate, Aadhaar of the deceased, and applicant ID
Registration is entered into the Civil Registration System
Certificate is issued digitally (QR-code signed) or physically, typically within 7 days for on-time registrations
source: Office of the Registrar General of India (CRS)

faq.question: What if the death wasn't registered within 21 days?
faq.answer: It can still be registered late with a delay fee (₹5-25 up to 1 year). Registration beyond 1 year additionally requires an order from a District Magistrate or the state-designated authority.

faq.question: Is the digital death certificate legally valid?
faq.answer: Yes — the CRS portal issues QR-code digitally signed certificates that are accepted for legal purposes including insurance claims, bank account closure, and property transfer.
